prose: George Hotz sets the record straight: he loves LLMs. After a hacking career (2007-2014) his whole working life has been AI, and he's giddy about the new models, self-driving cars, video generation and coding agents - a Linux box running opencode on a local GLM-5.2 that can 'install tmux with the geohot configuration' from a sentence is, for him, the long-promised Year of the Linux Desktop.

What he hates is two flavors of hype. First, negative-valence hype: the constant claim that a window is closing, that you'll fall hopelessly behind - mostly designed to make you feel bad and move to San Francisco. Second, the strawman leap from 'fancy autocomplete, smart compiler, better search engine' to light-cone-owning superintelligence where everything Changes in a flash. He'll bet everything that neither is true.
highlights: geohot: 'I love LLMs' - career has been AI since 2014.
Local GLM-5.2 + opencode already feels transformative.
Hates negative hype: windows closing, permanent underclass.
Both hype flavors mostly serve to make you feel bad.
